House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.2Contents3
New in 3.0
00 · Foundation

Version 1.0 was a warm off-white ground with a clay-orange accent. So is Anthropic's. RGB distance between the two grounds: 23. Between the two accents: 53. Under about 40 reads as the same colour.

Everything else followed from fixing that.

What changed, and why.

01 · The ground

True white, not warm paper

Warm off-white plus a clay accent is a recognisable palette and it is not ours. The ground is now #FFFFFF with #0A0E27 text — 19:1, the most readable combination available, and cold enough that nothing about it reads borrowed.

02 · The colour

Terracotta out, Cobalt in

Terracotta is gone — from the logo, the buttons, the accents, everywhere. Cobalt #1231D6 replaces it as the single brand colour, at 8.62:1 on white. It is the only colour that fills a button.

03 · The architecture

Four pillars, not three practices

Solutions is closed. House of Ichigo does training and advisory, on a platform. The four pillars — Learn, Build, Lead, Govern — are now the company's only taxonomy, and the only thing colour-coded.

04 · The layout

Rules, not boxes

The card grid is gone. Pages are built on an asymmetric rail with hairline rules, square corners, no shadows and a wide margin that stays empty. Ma 間 was always in the guide; now it is in the grid.

05 · The type

One face, not a pairing

Fraunces is retired. Manrope carries display, every heading and the whole interface; Inter Tight stays below 20px for long-form text and supplies the system's only italic. The accent word is now weight and colour, not a slant. Fonts are self-hosted — no CDN, so a PDF renders what the screen shows.

Unchanged: the 会 mark and its calligraphy. Ink. Cobalt and the pillar colours. The accent word. The voice. 3.2 changes one face and nothing else.

Version

This book
3.3
Supersedes
3.2
Unchanged
Palette · type · voice · Sections 08–09

Colours and the three-font stack are locked and untouched. This release is about composition, imagery and what gets measured.

What changed in 3.3

3.2 made the system consistent and checkable. It did not make it distinctive: a mono eyebrow, a hairline rule, one accent word and a tinted statistic card is the house style of every generated deck. 3.3 changes the slides, the imagery, the website and the platform so that HOI’s work cannot be mistaken for anyone else’s.

What changed

  • Slides. Twelve layouts redrawn as real slides on real content, in three layers: brushwork, scale, diagram. Type floor raised to 24 px body and nothing under 16 px; 3.2’s eyebrow was 12 px.
  • The mark. Traced to a vector and used at landscape scale on cover, divider and close.
  • The diagram kit. Gates, stages, pillars, dot field and the scoring quadrant, drawn with the engine’s own partition rather than a symmetric 2 × 2.
  • Imagery. Art direction: real sessions, real people, no stock and no generated images.
  • Website and platform. The hero shows the product. The platform is designed around the quadrant; three tinted KPI cards became one hero metric.
  • Measured. scripts/slide_gate.js opens the deck at 1280 × 720 and fails on clipped text, type under the floor, text touching the mark, low contrast, shadows, gradients and accent overuse.

Needs a decision

  • The mark at scale amends the logo rules. Clear space (1R) and “cover and close only”. Proposed: exempt from clear space, never from the 24 px text rule; divider added. Needs the brand owner.
  • Learn and Build are unchanged and still close to framework defaults. #0089A8 is 15 units from Tailwind cyan-600; #008558 is 14 from emerald-700. They now appear only as bars and 6 px dots, so moving them is cheap.
  • There are no real photographs yet. Every image slot is a labelled frame until the first shoot.
  • The website scorer is a proposal. It is drawn in the book and not built.

Retired

An eyebrow above every slide title · 12 px labels · 8% tinted statistic cards · three ruled columns as the default content slide · an accent phrase on every slide · grey wireframes as layout documentation.

00 · Foundation

会 — kai. Meeting, gathering, association. The ichie in ichigo ichie: one time, one meeting.

For a company that now only trains and advises, it reads better than it did when there was a build practice.

The house

House of Ichigo is a France-based, globally operating AI capability company. We make teams able to run AI themselves.

Equipped to run.

Equip is the core brand verb — tangible capability transfer, tools and knowledge and systems that stay behind. Never empower, enable or upskill. French: Équipés pour avancer.

Shokunin 職人

The craftsman's discipline. One team, one outcome.

Kaizen 改善

Continuous refinement. Build for evolution, not launch.

Ma 間

Meaningful space. What is left out sharpens what is there.

Ichigo ichie 一期一会

One time, one meeting. Each engagement is singular.

Never cherry blossoms, torii gates, calligraphy ornament, samurai imagery or any other Japanese motif. The 会 is custom artwork and is the single exception. The lineage is philosophical, not decorative.

We don't build or operate systems for clients. Your team builds. The platform holds the work. We make sure both are pointed at the right thing.

Platform

Company onboarding, AI maturity assessment, AI roadmap, governance flags. Generated, structured, re-runnable.

Advisory

Strategy papers and documents that turn the evidence into a committed course of action. Never anything that needs uptime.

Training

Three tiers per pillar — briefing, core, applied. Twelve programmes. No depth ladder, no published duration.

New in 3.0

A decision made in this version. Colour, architecture, layout, and everything that follows from them.

Carried forward

Established brand, unchanged. The mark, the voice, the Japanese lineage.

Changed in 3.2

How to read this book

Who it is for

  • The House of Ichigo team, on every surface they produce
  • Clients and partners co-branding with the house
  • White-label partners licensing the platform
  • Anyone briefing an agency or a freelancer

The one rule

Use the supplied assets and the tokens. If the thing you need does not exist, it gets added to the system — not improvised once in one artifact and forgotten.

Where the values actually live

This book is the human reference. tokens.json and tokens.css are what render. When they disagree with this book, they win.

A note on CMYK

CMYK figures are calculated from RGB and marked with an asterisk. They are indicative. Commission proper print builds before any four-colour job.

On contrast

Every ratio in Section 02 is measured to WCAG 2.1. Where a pairing is prohibited, it is prohibited on the number — not on taste.

New in 3.0
01 · Logo

Construction

The circle. A true circle, filled solid. Cobalt. Never a ring, never an ellipse, never a rounded square.

The character. Reversed out in white. Optically centred — it sits slightly high because the tail carries weight down.

The gap. The extremities stop short of the circle edge. That margin is artwork and is never reduced.

The mark

会 — kai

Meeting, gathering, association. It is drawn, not typeset: one brush gesture with a weighted opening stroke and a lifted tail. No font contains it as drawn, and no font should be used to fake it.

What changed

Only the fill. The path data is identical to 1.0. Anyone holding old collateral will recognise the new mark immediately, which is the point of recolouring rather than redrawing.

House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.301 · Logo10
Carried forward
01 · Logo

Components

1 · The mark. The 会 circle, centred above.

2 · The wordmark. HOUSE OF ICHIGO, letterspaced caps, ICHIGO set heavier. Artwork, not live type.

3 · The mark of origin. The © closing the wordmark. Never deleted, never enlarged.

The lockup

Fixed relationships

  • Wordmark width is locked to the circle diameter. Never adjust one without the other.
  • Scale as one group, proportionally, from a corner handle only.
  • Never re-set HOUSE OF ICHIGO in Inter Tight or anything else to stand in for the wordmark.
  • Never separate the mark from the wordmark and re-space them.

Mark-only use

Permitted on square avatars, favicons, app icons, and as the framing device on page 13. On slides it is landscape artwork on the cover, divider and close (see The mark at scale), never a corner mark. On any surface using the mark alone, the full lockup appears at least once.

House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.301 · Logo11
New in 3.0
01 · Logo

One artwork, two grounds.

A cobalt circle with a white 会 works on white and on Ink. Version 1.0 maintained four colourways — terracotta, navy, white, and white-on-terracotta. 3.0 maintains one, plus a single-colour version for processes that cannot hold it.

Primary
On white and on any light ground.
On Ink
The same file. No second artwork.
On Cool Grey
Panels and secondary surfaces.
Single colour
Ink. Engraving, fax, mono print, legal filings.

The luminance test

Convert the background to greyscale. Lighter than 55% grey or darker than 45% grey both take the primary lockup. Between the two, change the background or place the logo on a solid white or Ink block. Never add a shadow, glow or keyline to force legibility, and never place the lockup over a photograph without a solid holding block.

01 · Logo

The measure

R = the radius of the mark's circle. Clear space is 1R on all four sides of the lockup's bounding box. Because R scales with the logo, the rule works identically on a favicon and on a wall.

The inner line shows 0.5R — the absolute floor, used only where a physical edge makes 1R impossible.

Clear space

R
R
R
R

Nothing enters the clear zone

  • Type of any kind, including straplines and URLs
  • Other logos, partner marks, certification badges
  • Rules, boxes, keylines, page furniture
  • Photographic subjects or busy areas of an image
  • The trim edge, fold or perforation of a printed piece

In practice

  • Align the lockup to the layout margin and let the clear zone run past it.
  • Two logos side by side: clear zones do not overlap, and the larger R governs.
  • Ma 間 is a brand principle. If the logo feels tight, it is tight.
House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.301 · Logo13
Carried forward
01 · Logo

Why there is a floor

The wordmark is letterspaced at about 0.18em. Below 18mm lockup height that spacing collapses visually and HOUSE OF ICHIGO reads as a grey bar.

The brush tail on the 会 is the first thing to go. At 8mm the character still reads; below it, the negative space closes and the mark becomes a blob.

Minimum sizes

Full lockup at minimum reproduction size
MediumMinimum
Print — full lockup18 mm height
Screen — full lockup72 px height
Print — mark alone8 mm diameter
Screen — mark alone32 px diameter
ProcessMinimum
Embroidery25 mm
Screen print20 mm
Foil, emboss, deboss20 mm, mark only
Engraving15 mm, Ink single colour

If the space is smaller than the minimum, do not shrink the logo. Drop to the mark, or remove the logo and name the house in the text. A logo too small to read is worse than no logo.

The mark existed only as a 670 px raster, which capped it at about 56 mm at 300 dpi. It is now traced (build/trace_mark.py), with the two sharp notches kept sharp. It is a reproduction of the only artwork that exists, not a redraw: if the original vector is found, it replaces this file.

The mark at scale

The mark is a hand-brushed character in a circle: the one organic thing in a flat, mono system. 3.2 used it as a 24 px avatar. 3.3 uses it the way it cannot be copied: large, cropped, on three slide types.

  • Cropped, never floating. At least a quarter of the disc leaves the canvas.
  • Large. At least 62% of the slide width: 800 px on 1280.
  • Three colourways. White on Cobalt, Cobalt on Ink, Ink on Cobalt.
  • Cover, divider and close. One per slide; conviction and statistic stay pure type.
  • Text stays off it. 24 px to any text, and never over the strokes.

What they share

Each is an attempt to make the logo fit a layout rather than making the layout fit the logo. The mark has no tolerance for adjustment, and needs none.

Also prohibited

  • Reproducing the 会 in any typeface, including a Japanese one
  • Using the character outside the circle, or the circle alone as "the logo"
  • Animating the character as if it were being brushed
  • Placing a partner logo inside the clear zone

And

  • Sourcing the logo from a website screenshot or a slide export
  • Adding Japanese ornament near the mark
  • Filling the circle with a photograph or a pattern
  • Using a pillar colour for the logo — the logo is Cobalt or Ink, never Learn, Build or Lead
House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.301 · Logo17
New in 3.0
01 · Logo

Why this page exists

The logo has been stretched in production more than once. Both times the cause was the same: a logo image placed inside a flex column, where align-items:stretch silently overrides width:auto.

It is not a judgement failure. It is a CSS default, and it is prevented by a rule, not by care.

Placement & technical rules

Every logo image carries all four

img{width:auto;max-width:100%;
    align-self:flex-start;flex:0 0 auto}
.logo-lockup{aspect-ratio:670/790}
.logo-mark{aspect-ratio:1/1}
.centred{align-self:center}
  • width:auto — height drives the size, never width
  • align-self:flex-start — defeats the stretch default
  • flex:0 0 auto — the logo never grows or shrinks with its container
  • aspect-ratio — a second line of defence if the others are overridden

Exact proportions

Full lockup670 × 790 · 0.848 : 1
Mark alone670 × 669 · 1.0015 : 1

In other tools

PowerPointInsert, then set height only and let width follow. Never drag a side handle — corner handles only, with Shift held.
FigmaPlace as a component with proportions locked. Never a frame set to fill on both axes.
WordLock aspect ratio in Layout → Size before resizing.
EmailSet width and height attributes in the HTML, not in CSS. Some clients strip the CSS.
VideoPlace the SVG, never a scaled PNG. Check the first and last frame of any animation.

The check. The 会 circle is a true circle. If it reads as an oval at any size, on any surface, the logo has been distorted — stop and replace it. There is no tolerance and no exception.

The rule

Pillar colour is wayfinding, never decoration. If it is not telling you which pillar, it does not belong on the page.

Where it appears

  • The eyebrow above a heading
  • A 2.4px rule under a section head
  • A dot in platform navigation
  • An 8% tint on a panel
  • Chart series where the series are the pillars

Where it never does

  • Buttons — those are Cobalt
  • Body copy — that is Ink
  • Large filled areas
  • The logo
  • Two pillar colours at full strength on one surface

Govern is Ink

Govern does not get a fourth hue. It takes Ink, which is the most authoritative value in the system and semantically right for the pillar about control and limits. It also keeps the palette at three chromatic colours plus the brand.

Tints and surfaces

How a tint is built

Base colour mixed with white at the stated percentage. No hue shift. Never use a tint of one pillar colour to approximate another.

The working value

8% is the panel tint. Ink on an 8% pillar tint measures about 17:1 — comfortable for long reading.

Anything between 22% and 70% is a chart range, never a surface.

Fatigue

Fatigue does not come from bright colour. It comes from bright colour over large areas. Cobalt is vivid precisely because there is so little of it.

The two failures

Swatch board. Cobalt and three pillar colours on one page. The system distinguishes; it does not fill.

Grey house. Ink and white only. Correct, inert, indistinguishable from a legal document.

Proportion

White & Cool Grey — 70%
Ink — 22%
8%

70 / 22 / 8 — ground, text and dark surfaces, colour. Ma 間 is counted in the 70: margins and clear space are part of the composition, not what is left over.

SurfaceRatioThe 8% is
Website and digital70 / 22 / 8Cobalt
Catalogue and brochure70 / 22 / 8Pillar colour per spread, Cobalt for actions
Training decks72 / 22 / 6That pillar's colour
Advisory papers78 / 20 / 2Cobalt on the cover only
RFP and proposals78 / 20 / 2Cobalt on the cover only
Platform UI70 / 22 / 8Pillar colour for wayfinding, Cobalt for actions

On a pillar-owned surface the pillar colour takes the 8%. Cobalt then reduces to two things: the logo and the action. It does not disappear and it does not share the accent share at full strength.

Contrast — measured

Standard

WCAG 2.1 relative luminance. AA is the minimum for every surface. AAA is the target for body copy. Large text means 18pt regular or 14pt bold and above — it needs 3:1, not 4.5:1.

Beyond contrast

  • Colour never carries meaning alone — a pillar colour always appears with the pillar name
  • Body minimum 9pt print, 16px screen
  • Targets 44 × 44px with a visible Cobalt focus ring

Setting rules

Alignment

  • Left-ranged, ragged right. Never justified
  • Measure 45–75 characters
  • No hyphenation in headings
  • Centred type on covers and single-line convictions only

Case & emphasis

  • Bold is Inter Tight 600 or 700

  • Colour is not emphasis

Numbers

  • All figures in JetBrains Mono, tabular

Punctuation

  • Curly quotes and apostrophes, never straight
  • En dash for ranges, em dash for asides
  • One space after a full stop
  • No exclamation marks on corporate surfaces
  • No emoji anywhere

The one-minute check

  1. Are all three fonts doing only their own job?
  2. Is negative tracking set on every display line 24px and above?
  3. Exactly one accent word per heading — or none, per the family table?
  4. Are all data numerals mono?
  5. Does any line run past 90 characters?
  6. Is the ground white, and is the margin still empty?

Voice

The brand is recognisable in writing before it is recognisable in design. Short, declarative, evidence-led, and specific about which verbs it will and will not use.

  • Principles
  • The word family
  • Banned language
  • Tone by family

House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.304 · Voice35
Carried forward
04 · Voice

The core verb

equip.

Equip, equipped, equipping. Tangible capability transfer — tools, knowledge and systems that stay behind after the engagement ends.

Never empower, enable or upskill. The first two are vague, the third is passive, and all three are what everyone else says.

Principles

How it sounds

  • Short, declarative sentences. Twelve words average
  • Present tense for capabilities. "We build", not "we can build"
  • Evidence-led. Real numbers, real sources. No promise without a measurable outcome
  • No hedging. No could, might, potentially
  • End with a next action. Every section closes on something the reader can do

Verbs

Use: deploy · build · ship · execute · run · govern · equip · scope · validate · evaluate · monitor

Avoid: discover · explore · unlock · transform

Spectator verbs — they describe watching from the sidelines. Replace with practitioner verbs.

Person

  • Website uses second person in value statements
  • Proposals use we for the house, you for the client
  • No first-person singular anywhere

Tone by family

FamilyRegisterItalic accent RatioWhat it must never do
Website & digitalEditorial, executive, confident Every H1 / H270/22/8 Read as a SaaS landing page. No feature grid of icons with three-word benefits.
Catalogue & brochureClear, structured, comparable One per spread70/22/8 Bury the ladder. A buyer must see four pillars and four depths without reading prose.
BD & salesConsultative, evidence-led One per major heading70/22/8 Promise an outcome without a number attached.
Training decksInstructional, grounded, encouraging Cover and outro only72/22/6 Sell. Body content teaches; marketing flourishes distract learners.
Advisory papersPrecise, neutral, defensible Cover title only78/20/2 Editorialise. The client reuses this without us in the room.
RFP & proposalsStructured, compliant, evidence-led Excluded entirely78/20/2 Deviate from the requested structure. Compliance first, voice second.

Why the accent narrows

The accent word is a marketing device. The further a surface sits from selling and the closer to teaching or contracting, the less of it there is — until in an RFP there is none.

Why the ratio tightens

Same logic in colour. A website carries 8% Cobalt. An advisory paper carries 2%, on the cover, because the reader is evaluating evidence and every flourish costs credibility.

When a surface is ambiguous

Ask who is reading and why. Reading to buy → website, catalogue or BD. Reading to learn → training. Reading to verify → advisory or RFP. If two apply, use the tighter one.

05 · Composition

This page is the example

You are reading the rail now. The narrow column carries the eyebrow, the aside and the caveat. The wide column carries the argument. Neither is centred, and the two are never equal.

Why asymmetry

Equal columns and evenly spaced cards are the default output of every layout tool and every generated interface. An unequal grid reads as a decision.

The rail

A two-column grid at roughly 1:3. The narrow rail holds marginalia — eyebrow, section number, notes, caveats, definitions. The wide column holds the content. Every page in this book uses it, and every House of Ichigo document should.

Rail collapses; use the full width

Rules

  • The rail may be empty. It is not a container to fill
  • Never put the primary argument in the rail
  • On mobile the rail stacks above the main column, never below
  • Rail text is 6.9pt / 12px, Slate

05 · Composition

No glow

Version 1.0 permitted a terracotta radial glow on dark covers. It is withdrawn. 3.0 has no gradients at all — Ink surfaces are flat.

On Ink

Body text is white. Secondary text is white at 55–60% opacity — never Slate, which measures 3.19:1 and fails. Cobalt on Ink is 2.20:1, so the accent word lightens to a Cobalt tint on dark surfaces.

Dark rhythm

Ink is punctuation. It marks the moments where the argument turns, and it stops working the moment it becomes the default.

Conviction
We don't teach tools. We teach execution.

Where Ink belongs

  • Covers and title slides
  • Section dividers
  • Conviction and pull-quote blocks
  • The closing or call-to-action section
  • Govern-pillar material
  • Platform chrome — sidebar and top bar

Where it does not

  • Body-heavy content pages
  • Tables and data
  • Two consecutive sections
  • Training module bodies
  • Advisory papers — those are white throughout

Cadence

On a web page, one Ink section per two or three white ones. In a deck, an Ink slide every five to seven — cover, dividers, the one conviction, the close. If two Ink surfaces end up adjacent, one of them is not earning it.

Grid & layout

Grids by surface

SurfaceColumnsGutterMargin
Web — desktop1224 px64 px · 1280 max

Composition rules

  • One idea per surface. A page that needs "and" is two pages
  • Asymmetry over centring. Content ranges left against a generous right margin; centred layouts are covers only
  • Three levels of hierarchy maximum
  • Never eat the margin. If a layout only works by encroaching, the content is too long

Vertical structure — every surface, every format

Head — eyebrow + title. Fixed height, never grows
Body — fills all remaining height. Centred, top-aligned or spread
Foot — one line. Source, folio, or nothing

The body is the only part that flexes. Three modes: centred for a single statement, top for a list that may run short, spread when a footnote or action must sit at the base.

Content stacked at the top of a surface with a void beneath it is the most common layout defect. It is always a missing flex rule on the body, never a content problem.

Density ceilings

5 bullets per slide at 12 words · 4 columns per row · 6 table columns · 4 chart series · 6 nav items · 10–16 slides per deck · 45–75 characters per line. Ceilings, not targets.

05 · Composition

Imagery

Subject

  • Real people in real work contexts — workshops, screens, whiteboards, classrooms, factory floors
  • Candid rather than posed. Concentration, discussion, working hands
  • The client's world, not a generic office
  • Where people are not the subject, show the artefact — a process map, a dashboard, a plan

Treatment

  • Natural light. Honest grading, full colour
  • No duotone, no brand-colour wash, no tint
  • Photography under type carries a 20% Ink scrim, never a blur
  • Crops are 16:9, 4:3, square, or the circle framing device
  • Never blue-tinted — that is the tech-stock signature we are avoiding

Never

  • Neural networks, glowing brains, circuit-board overlays
  • Robot hands, humanoid robots, android faces
  • Blue tech aurora, particle fields, data streams
  • Cherry blossoms, torii gates, calligraphy ornament
  • Handshake-over-cityscape and other stock clichés
  • AI-generated images of people on any client-facing surface

The substitution rule

If no honest photograph exists, do not reach for a stock abstraction. Use a diagram, a data visualisation, a large statistic, or space. An empty, well-set surface is always better than a decorative image that says nothing.

Rights

Every image of a person needs a release and every client site a location clearance. Client work shown publicly needs written sign-off, including anything identifiable in the background of a workshop photo.

Image layouts

Five layouts. Every image on every surface uses one of them — there is no sixth, and no free placement.

Title here

01 · Full bleed + scrim

Image to the edges, flat Ink scrim at 78%, white type. Covers, section openers, campaign key visuals. The scrim is flat — never a gradient.

Portrait 1200×1440
Heading
Body copy sits in the wider half.

02 · Split, 46 / 54

Image full-height on one side. The asymmetric variant of the rail, for wide canvases. Image left by default; right only to vary a sequence.

Interface capture sits in a plain chrome frame — no shadow, no perspective, no device mockup.

03 · Screenshot frame

1px Line border, simple chrome bar. Product and tool captures. Never a laptop mockup, never angled, never with a reflection.

04 · Video holding frame

Ink field, white play mark, mono spec label, caption beneath. Demos, screen recordings, session playback.

Before
After

05 · Comparison pair

Two equal frames, captioned beneath each. Before and after, ungrounded and grounded, option A and option B. Never three.

Rules for all five

  • Captions are mono, 11 px / 6.9 pt, Slate, below the image — never inside it
  • No rounded corners, no shadows, no borders except the screenshot frame
  • Type over an image needs the 78% Ink scrim, or a solid holding block. Never a blur
  • One image layout per surface
  • Placeholders carry their own spec in mono, so whoever fills them knows the dimension

Delivery sizes

Full bleed 2560×1440 · Split portrait 1200×1440 · Screenshot 2× native · Video frame 1920×1080 · Comparison 1200×900 each.

What a HOI photograph is

Subject
People at work
Light
As found
Treatment
None
Source
HOI sessions only
Consent
Written, each person

Confirm with the client what may be published before you photograph, and in the Gulf and Africa sessions confirm it locally: what is fine in Paris is not automatically fine in Riyadh.

Art direction

The most un-generated thing HOI has is proof of humans: four thousand people in five hundred companies. A photograph of a real session says what no illustration can.

Never

  • Stock photography, of any kind
  • Generated imagery, of any kind, on any surface
  • Isometric or 3D illustration
  • Neural networks, glowing brains, robot hands, blue aurora, particle fields
  • Handshakes over a cityscape
  • Colour grading, duotone, or any filter: cropping only, and only through the five image layouts

Why this and not a look

A treatment can be applied by anyone in a minute, so it cannot be a differentiator. A real photograph of a real room cannot be applied by anyone, so it can. Until the first shoot, every image slot is a labelled frame: no image beats a wrong one.

05 · Composition

Construction

Outline only. 1.6px stroke on a 24px grid, scaling proportionally. Square joins where the form is architectural, round caps on open ends.

Geometric and reductive, to match the type. Never illustrative, never hand-drawn, never filled.

Colour

Ink by default · white on Ink · the pillar colour on a pillar-owned surface · Cobalt only inside an action. One colour per icon, always flat.

Iconography

Version 1.0 had no icon system, so every deck sourced icons from wherever. A single foreign icon is visible immediately in a set this consistent.

04 · Two column

A claim at 80 px, weight against weight, and the reasoning at reading size.

Rules

  • Nothing is clipped, ever. Type at scale is the picture: a cropped plus sign changes the number.
  • Body copy is 24 px or larger; anything under 20 px is a label and is mono.
  • One idea per slide, and the headline is the idea. “Overview” is a label, not a claim.
  • Weight contrast before colour contrast. 800 against 300 on one line.
  • Centred text is not used. Everything ranges left on the 72 px margin.

Measured

scripts/slide_gate.js opens the deck at 1280 × 720 and fails on text that leaves the slide, type under the floor, body copy under 24 px, text within 24 px of the mark, contrast under 4.5:1 (3:1 at 24 px and above), a box-shadow, a gradient, a second mark, or two accent phrases inside five slides. Its self-test breaks the deck six ways and requires the gate to name each one.

07 · Quadrant

Business impact against delivery readiness, drawn with the scoring engine’s own partition.

The quadrant is not a 2 × 2. Delivery readiness under 50 is “Fix foundations first” at any impact. House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.306 · Applications62
New in 3.0
06 · Applications

Where it sits

The Use-Case Portfolio ranks. The blueprint specifies one of them, in enough detail for the client's team to build it.

The boundary

It specifies what and why, and stops where implementation begins. It is not a technical specification, and House of Ichigo does not build from it.

Use-case blueprint

Four pages, fixed structure. The structure is the discipline — a use case that cannot fill these sections is not ready to build.

01 · Cover and summary

Identifier, score, stage, governance flag, make-or-buy, effort, prerequisites. Then the whole thing in one paragraph: what happens today, what would happen instead, what that is worth.

02 · The process today

Step table with who, which system and how long. Volume and time in the rail. Where it breaks and what it costs — with a number.

03 · What is proposed

One sentence with no tool names in it. Step-by-step, marking what is automated and what a human decides. Data required, systems touched, and an explicit out-of-scope list.

04 · Governance, success, ownership

AI Act tier, personal data, transparency, retention. Success measures with a baseline and who measures them. A named owner with time allocated, and what must be true before build starts.

Rules

  • Ratio 78 / 20 / 2. No accent word after the cover title
  • Every figure mono, every estimate marked as an estimate
  • The out-of-scope list is mandatory — it is what stops drift
  • "Your team builds this" appears on the cover, not buried

Never

  • Name a vendor or a model in the proposal section
  • Write an architecture, a schema or pseudo-code
  • Estimate an implementation timeline — only the effort to be ready
  • Issue one without a named owner
House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.306 · Applications63
New in 3.0
06 · Applications

What it is

The record the client signs. It closes an engagement and it is the document either party reaches for if there is a disagreement later.

Why no accent

This is the one document with no accent word at all, including the cover. A contractual record that reads persuasive reads as if it is selling something.

Client validation dossier

Five sections. Committed against delivered, the evidence, the decisions, the handover, and two signatures.

01 · Scope as agreed

Committed / delivered / evidence / status, line by line. Changes during the engagement, with who requested them. And what was not delivered, and why.

02 · Evidence base

Every artefact with its source, date, capturer and reference. Limits of the evidence. Participation figures. All reproducible from the platform.

03 · Decisions & handover

What was decided and by whom. What was handed over, to which named owner, in what format, and where it lives. Open items the client now owns.

04 · Validation

Two signature blocks, client and house. Name, role, date. Above them, one sentence stating exactly what signing confirms.

The closing line is fixed: this dossier is a record of delivery, not a warranty of outcome.

The section that earns its keep

"Not delivered, and why." Most validation documents omit it, which is how a small gap becomes a dispute. Being explicit costs one paragraph and settles the question permanently.

If something is wrong, the client marks the line and returns it unsigned. Corrections happen before signature, never after.

Ratio 78 / 20 / 2 · A4 portrait · 42 mm rail · no Ink pages · all figures mono. Template ships as templates/validation-dossier.html.

Do and don't

Do

  • Start from the supplied logo files and the tokens — never a screenshot or a hex from memory
  • Set every surface on white or Ink. Never a warm off-white
  • Hold 70 / 22 / 8, tightening to 78 / 20 / 2 on advisory papers and RFPs
  • Give the surface one accent: Cobalt, or the pillar colour if a pillar owns it
  • Keep every primary button Cobalt, on every surface, including pillar-owned ones
  • Set exactly one accent word per display heading — or none, per the family table
  • Set negative tracking on every display line 24px and above
  • Put every numeral in JetBrains Mono, tabular
  • Keep 1R of clear space around the logo
  • Use the rail. Leave it empty when there is nothing to say
  • Check any new type-on-colour pairing against page 21
  • Add a missing asset to the system rather than improvising it once

Don't

  • Use terracotta anywhere. It is retired
  • Redraw, recolour, rotate, stretch or crop the mark, or re-set the 会 in any font
  • Set a warm off-white ground, or any cream, ivory or paper tint
  • Set white text on Warning, or Slate text on Ink
  • Set body copy in Cobalt or any pillar colour
  • Use two pillar colours at full strength on one surface — except platform navigation
  • Use a pillar colour for a button
  • Add a fourth font, for any reason
  • Use Inter Tight italic, or more than one accent word per heading
  • Add gradients, drop shadows, glows, or radii above 2px
  • Build a card grid. Use rules and the rail
  • Show neural networks, robot hands, blue tech aurora, or any Japanese motif
  • Write transformative, unlock, empower, or anything on page 34

House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.307 · Governance72
New in 3.0
07 · Governance

Why this page

Most work on this brand will be produced with an AI assistant. A brand book it cannot parse is a brand book it will not follow.

Every rule in this document also exists as a machine-readable file, and those files are the ones to give a model.

Machine-readable spec

The package

FileGive it to
BRAND.mdAny AI assistant, as a system prompt or project instruction. The complete rule set in ~1,800 words
tokens.jsonCode generation. Every colour, size, ratio and constraint, with measured contrast
tokens.cssAny web or HTML output. Custom properties plus base component classes
patterns.htmlCopy-paste reference for every component and layout in this book
brand_check.pyRun on any output before it ships. Exits non-zero on a violation
assets/Logo files with their exact aspect ratios recorded

The instruction that works

"Follow BRAND.md exactly. Use only tokens.json values.
Copy structures from patterns.html rather than inventing
them. Run brand_check.py before presenting output."

What the checker catches

  • Any hex outside the palette, its tints, or neutral greys
  • Retired values — terracotta, warm paper, the old navy, the four Tailwind tokens
  • Unapproved font names · any fonts.googleapis.com link · a synthesised italic
  • Logo images missing the aspect-ratio guard
  • Prohibited pairings — white on Warning, Slate on Ink
  • Banned vocabulary in body copy
  • Rounded corners above 2 px, gradients, box-shadows

What it cannot catch

Proportion, restraint, whether the margin is doing its work, whether a heading is a claim or a label, and whether an image earns its place. Those still need a person. The checker removes the mechanical failures so the review can be about the design.

Migrating from 1.0

This is a rebrand, so it cannot be done entirely by find-and-replace. But nothing needs recalling, and the mark is unchanged — a 1.0 artifact and a 3.0 artifact still read as the same company.

#ActionFind → replaceEffortWhy
1Swap the logo files All terracotta / navy lockups → cobalt lockupMechanical One artwork replaces four colourways. Same 会, so recognition carries.
2Swap the ground #FAFAF7 → #FFFFFFMechanical The single change that removes the resemblance. Do it first.
3Swap the accent #CF5B2B → #1231D6
#1E2B4D → #0A0E27		Mechanical Terracotta retires. Navy folds into Ink. Fixes the failing 1.0 link contrast at the same time.
4Retire the Tailwind tokens #3B82F6 #0891B2 #F59E0B #DC2626Mechanical Replaced by Cobalt, Build, Warning and Danger.
5Rewrite the architecture "three practices, one platform" → "four pillars, two ways in, one platform"Copy pass Solutions is closed. Anything naming it is out of date, not just off-brand.
6Rebuild the layout Card grids → rail and rulesPer template Do this as each template is next opened. The card grid is the strongest remaining tell.

Do first

The website and the platform. That is where the ground colour and the link colour are most visible, and where a half-migrated brand is most obvious.

Safe to leave

Anything printed and anything already with a client. Steps 1–4 are invisible in isolation; a client holding a 1.0 deck will not notice until they see a 3.0 one beside it.

Do announce it

Unlike a token refresh, this one is worth saying out loud. The colour changed because the company changed — training and advisory, four pillars, one platform. The rebrand is the proof of the repositioning.

08 · Interface

Elevation, without a single shadow

3.2 has no box-shadow at any level. Separation comes from surface, border weight and a scrim.

e0 · ground

the page itself, and anything sitting flat on it

border none

e1 · raised

panels, cards-that-are-not-cards, a section that needs edges

border 1px #E3E8EF

e2 · overlay

menus, popovers, dropdowns, tooltips, the command palette

border 1px #0A0E27

e3 · modal

dialogs, sheets, anything that takes the whole screen hostage

border 1.6px #0A0E27

An Ink hairline is 19:1 against white. It separates harder than any soft shadow, and unlike a shadow it survives print, a 1x display and a dark ground. A shadow is a picture of depth; a border is depth you can measure.

The density contract

DATA TABLES ONLY, at 25 rows or more. Never for a form, never for navigation.

One scale per container

Set the class on a container and the children inherit. Never mix scales inside one panel — two row heights in one table reads as a rendering bug, not as emphasis. compact is the default when nothing is set.

Print sizes are not product sizes

The scale in section 03 is for paper, where 9.2pt body and generous leading are correct. Carried into the product they make a 41-row table unusable. The two scales are deliberately separate and neither is a fallback for the other.

House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.308 · Interface79
New in 3.2
08 · Interface

The rule

  • :focus-visible, never :focus
  • Ring 2px solid #1231D6, offset 2px
  • Inset to −2px where a scroll container would clip it
  • On Ink the ring is #7FA0FF — 7.58:1 against Ink
  • outline:none without a replacement is a defect, not a style choice

Focus and hit area

Focused

On white and on Cobalt the ring is Cobalt at 8.62:1.

Focused on Ink

On Ink it switches to Cobalt Light at 7.58:1. Cobalt on Ink would not be visible.

44 × 44, always

WCAG 2.5.5. A 28px dense row is legal because the row is not the target — the control inside it is, and it still needs 44 × 44.

Reach it with padding or a pseudo-element that extends the hit area beyond the visible box. Never by growing the row: that silently converts a dense table back into a compact one.

Visible mark 16px, hit area 44px. The dashed edge is the target, not the ink.

New in 3.2
08 · Interface

Motion, and the absence of it

Duration

instant0 msno transition at all
fast120 ms
base180 ms
slow260 ms
deliberate400 ms

Easing

standardcubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)
entercubic-bezier(0,0,0,1)
exitcubic-bezier(.3,0,1,1)

Assignments

colour and opacityfast
overlay enterbase, enter
overlay exitfast, exit
panel or drawerslow
progress and skeletondeliberate, looping

Nothing in the product is slower than 400ms. Past that the interface is performing rather than responding.

Prohibited

  • anything over 400ms
  • bounce, spring, overshoot or elastic easing
  • parallax, and movement tied to scroll position
  • transform on press — a button does not shrink
  • animating layout properties (width, height, top, left); use opacity and transform

Reduced motion is not a nicety. @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) — every duration drops to 0ms except opacity, which keeps `fast`. This is not optional and it is not a nicety. Around a third of adults over 40 have had some vestibular dysfunction; for them the alternative to this setting is nausea, not a preference about taste.

The two that matter

A placeholder is not a label. It disappears the moment someone types and takes the question with it. Anyone who looks away mid-form comes back to a box of text with no name on it.

Validate on blur, not on keystroke. Telling someone their email is wrong while they are still typing it is a sentence read aloud before it is finished.

Forms

Work email
We send the assessment link here. It is not added to any list.
name@company.com
Team size optional
12
The field is the width of its answer.
Department
 
Choose the department this assessment covers — it decides which benchmark you are compared against.

Rules

labelabove the field, always. Never a placeholder as a label — it disappears the moment someone types and takes the question with it.
placeholderan example of the answer, or nothing
helpbelow the label, above the field, Slate 13px. It is read before the mistake, not after.
requiredmark the OPTIONAL ones. If most fields are required, a required marker is noise on every row.
errorbelow the field, danger text, and it says what to do — not 'invalid input'. The field also gets aria-invalid and a danger border.
validation timingon blur, never on keystroke. Telling someone their email is wrong while they are typing it is a sentence read aloud before it is finished.
widththe field is the width of its answer. A postcode field the width of the page is a question you are asking badly.
groupfieldset + legend for radio and checkbox groups. Not a div.

Rules

itemone question per row: number, question, scale. The number is mono, the question is body text, the scale is the control.
scale5 points, labelled at both ends and in the middle. An unlabelled 5-point scale collects noise.

Why a bar is not enough

A progress bar at 30% hides whether seven questions are left or seventy. "Question 7 of 24" is the same information without the guess, and it is the difference between someone finishing and someone closing the tab.

Comfortable, always

48px rows, 16px text. This is the surface a first-time user meets, often on a phone, often once. It is the one screen that never gets compacted.

Rules

headermono, 11px, uppercase, .14em, Slate, 1.2px Ink rule beneath
rows1px Line rule between. No zebra striping — the rule is the separator, and stripes fight the rail.
numeralsJetBrains Mono, tabular, right-aligned. Always.

Why no stripes

Zebra striping is a second separator doing the job the hairline already does, and the grey bands fight the rail that carries every other page. One rule between rows, and the eye follows it.

The empty cell

An en dash. Not a blank — a blank looks like a rendering fault. Not "N/A" — it takes the width of real data and says less than a dash.

Alignment

Text left, numerals right and mono and tabular. A centred column has no edge to scan down, which is the only reason to put data in a table.

A red/amber/green scale would import a traffic-light language the brand does not have, collide with the pillar colours, and make a low maturity score look like a fault when it is a starting position. A client at 2.1 is not failing; they are at the beginning.

The rule

Cobalt on a grey track, at every value. The number is Manrope, tabular. The band is a WORD, never a colour.

On a pillar screen

On a pillar-owned screen the fill may take the pillar colour, once, for that pillar's own score. Never two pillar colours in one chart — that is a legend, and a legend means the chart failed.

The six criteria

The vendor scorecard scores six criteria. They are criteria, never pillars — "pillar" means Learn, Build, Lead or Govern and nothing else, on every surface.

Badges and the stepper

EU AI Act tier

UnacceptableHighLimitedMinimal

Governance flag

BlockedReviewCleared

Fill is earned, not decorative. A badge takes a fill only when it needs a human to act. Limited and Minimal carry no fill because nothing needs doing about them. A screen where every badge is coloured has told you nothing about which one to open.

No success colour

3.1 carried a --success token at #008558 — the same hex as the Build pillar. One green meant both "the Build pillar owns this" and "this passed", on screens that show both.

It is retired. Success is Ink text and the word. Nothing in this system needs a colour to announce that it is fine.

Use cases
Forty-one mapped

The one dark area

The sidebar is the only large Ink area in the product. It anchors the screen; everything else is white so the content carries the weight.

Two widths

232px expanded, 64px collapsed. No intermediate state. A drag-resizable sidebar is a preference nobody has and a layout nobody tested.

Current, not active

The current page is white at 100% with a 2px Cobalt leading edge, and carries aria-current. Rest is white at 60% — never Slate, which is 2.59:1 on Ink.

House of Ichigo · Brand Book 3.308 · Interface87
New in 3.2
08 · Interface

Empty, loading, error

Three states that get designed last and seen first. A new client meets the empty state before they meet anything else in the product.

No use cases mapped yet
Mapping turns a process into something the scoring engine can read. Start with the one that takes the most hours.
Map a use case

empty

Say what goes here and give the action that puts it there.

Never: an illustration, a shrug, or 'No data'.

loading

A skeleton at the shape of what is arriving.

Never: a spinner where the shape is known; a blank screen; a layout that jumps when content lands

The scoring engine did not return
Your answers are saved. Nothing has been lost and nothing has been scored. This usually clears within a minute.
Try again

error

What failed, what it means, what to do next. In that order.

Never: an error code alone, an apology without a next step, or a danger fill on a whole panel

Every one of the three ends in an action. An empty state without a button is a dead end; an error without a next step is an apology. The question each answers is not "what happened" but "what do I do now".

The contract

Esccloses the topmost overlay, and only the topmost
Tabstays inside a dialog or drawer; leaves a menu or popover
Arrow keysmove between items in a menu, a select or the palette
Enteractivates the focused item
Home / Endfirst and last item in a list
typingtype-ahead in a select; a query in the palette

The keyboard contract

  • One overlay at a time, with one exception: a confirm dialog may open over a drawer. Nothing else stacks.
  • Focus returns to the element that opened it. Losing focus to the page body is the most common keyboard bug in a product like this.
  • An overlay never holds the only copy of something. A dialog that disappears with unsaved work in it is a data-loss bug wearing a dismiss button.
  • No shadow at any level — see Section 08, elevation. A menu is a white surface with an Ink hairline.
  • Position by the trigger, flipping to stay on screen. Never centred except a dialog.

Select and combobox

closedlooks exactly like a text field — same height, same border, same focus ring. A control that acts like a field must look like one.
opene2 list, max 8 items visible, scroll beyond
searchappears at 10 options or more, automatically
multichips inside the field, each removable, count when it overflows one line
nevera native

Everything on this page is behaviour a headless primitive already implements correctly. Take the behaviour from a library and the appearance from these tokens. Re-implementing a focus trap by hand is how a product ships one that half works.

Which of our mapped use cases would fail the governance check?

AI Transformation Platform

Rules

alignmentright-aligned is prohibited. Both sides are left-aligned on the same measure; the speaker is named in mono above the message. Alternating alignment halves the reading measure and turns a transcript into a chat toy.
person labelmono, 11px, uppercase, Slate

The citation chip

chipmono superscript numeral in Cobalt, a 4px-radius outline chip on hover, opening the source panel on click

Messages and disclosure

toast

confirmation that something finished — saved, exported, sent

Shape: e2, bottom-left, one line, 5 seconds, dismissible

Never: an error that needs action. If the person must do something, it belongs where the thing is, not in a box that leaves on its own.

inline

anything the person must act on — a failed field, a blocked gate, an expired token

Shape: danger rule on the leading edge, next to what it concerns

Never: a page-wide danger fill

banner

a condition affecting the whole screen — read-only mode, a scheduled outage, a trial ending

Shape: full width, attention fill, Ink text, one action, dismissible only if it is not blocking

Never: more than one at a time

Disclosure controls

tabsfor peer views of the same object. Never for steps — that is the stepper. The current tab carries a 2px Cobalt bottom rule and aria-selected.
accordionhairline rows, chevron rotating 90 degrees over var(--dur-fast). No card, no fill, no shadow. Several may be open at once unless the content is mutually exclusive.
slidera 2px Line track, Cobalt fill to the left of the thumb, a 20px Ink thumb at 4px radius. The value is always shown as a numeral beside it — a slider without a readout is a guess.
togglefor a setting that applies immediately. A checkbox is for something that applies when the form is submitted. The two are not interchangeable and picking the wrong one is how a product gets a 'save' button nobody trusts.

A toggle applies immediately; a checkbox applies on submit. They are not interchangeable, and choosing the wrong one is how a product ends up with a save button nobody trusts.

09 · Experience

Six principles

The work is the evidence

Every screen ends in something a client can show their board: a score with its inputs, a blueprint, a flag with a reason. A screen that only informs is a screen that gets closed.

Say what will happen before it happens

Destructive and irreversible actions name their consequence in the button, not in a dialog title. 'Discard eight components' beats 'Are you sure?'

The person is never the one who has to remember

Answers save on change, filters persist, a half-finished assessment resumes where it stopped. Nothing asks twice for something already given.

Progress is stated, not implied

Six named stages, 'question 7 of 24', a scoring run that says which use case it is on. A spinner is the absence of this.

Nothing generated is applied without a human

The platform proposes; a person commits. This is the product promise and the governance position at once.

Slow is acceptable, silent is not

A scoring run may take a minute. It may not take a minute without saying what it is doing and letting the person leave and come back.

These decide arguments. When two designs are defensible, the one that leaves the client holding evidence wins; when a shortcut removes a human from a generated decision, it loses, whatever it saves.

This is the only stage with no prior investment to lose, so it is the one that must never feel like data entry.

The error taxonomy

Six classes. Every failure in the product is one of them, and the class decides where the message goes and what it says.

ClassCauseWhere it appearsWhat it saysNever
inputthe person typed something the system cannot acceptunder the fieldwhat is wrong and what a correct answer looks like'Invalid input'. Name the rule.
permissionthe person is not allowed to do thisin place of the control, not after pressing itwho can, and how to ask themshowing a control that always fails
absentthe thing does not exist, or no longer doesthe whole panelwhat was expected here and the nearest way backa bare 404
conflictsomeone else changed it firsta dialog, because it needs a decisionwhat changed, who changed it, and the two optionssilently overwriting either version
transientthe system failed and will probably work shortlyinline, next to what failedthat the work is saved, and offers a retrylosing the input. The retry must not require retyping.
modelthe model could not answer, or answered without groundsin the answer itselfwhich part is ungrounded and what would ground ita confident sentence with nothing behind it

The test

Read the message without the screen around it. If it does not say what to do next, it is not finished. "Something went wrong" fails this every time.

Never blame the person

"You entered an invalid date" and "Dates go in as 14/03/2027" carry the same information. One of them also tells them how to fix it.

New in 3.2
09 · Experience

The promise

The platform proposes; a person commits. This is the product promise and the governance position at the same time, and it is the reason a regulated buyer can adopt it.

Two gates

Gate 1 — is it safe to build? Gate 2 — is it safe to deploy? Both are steps a named person completes. Neither is ever crossed automatically.

Working with a model

uncertaintyShown per claim, not per screen. A chip, or the word ungrounded. Never a global confidence percentage — a single number over a mixed answer is a number about nothing.
latencyUnder 1s: nothing. 1-10s: a skeleton at the shape of the result. Over 10s: a named task the person can leave and return to, with a notification when it lands.
checkpointGate 1 before build, Gate 2 before deploy — the two gates in the offering, rendered as an explicit step a named person completes. The platform never crosses either on its own.
correctionEvery generated field is editable in place, and an edit is recorded as the person's, not the model's. The distinction survives into the export.
refusalWhen the model will not answer, the screen says what it will not do and what the person can do instead. A blank response is a defect.
attributionGenerated content is labelled where it appears and in the export. A client presenting a board paper must be able to say which sentences came from where.

Uncertainty is shown per claim, never per screen. A single confidence percentage over a mixed answer is a number about nothing — it cannot be acted on, and it invites the reader to trust the whole thing or none of it. The chip marks the sentence.

09 · Experience

Accessibility, and what is actually tested

The target

WCAG 2.2 level AA, and it is a commitment, not an aspiration — European public-sector buyers ask for it in writing.

Tested, every release

  • keyboard only, no mouse, every flow end to end
  • a screen reader on the questionnaire and the scorecard
  • 200% browser zoom with no horizontal scroll
  • contrast, measured, against the tokens rather than by eye
  • prefers-reduced-motion honoured
structureone h1 per screen, headings in order, landmarks named, every control labelled — a placeholder is not a label
statusaria-live polite for a score that arrives, assertive for a failure that stops work; never both on one region
motionevery duration drops to 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion except opacity

What is not claimed

Level AAA. Several AAA criteria conflict with a dense data product, and claiming what is not tested is worse than claiming less.

European public-sector buyers ask for AA in writing, so this is a commercial requirement before it is anything else. An untested claim of conformance is worse than a tested claim of less.

Why not Cairo

SEVEN uses Cairo. That is right for SEVEN and wrong here: their type is set large and loose, ours is set in 28px table rows.

Not a translation layer

Arabic is a locale, not a translation pass. Copy is written in Arabic, not translated from English at the end, and the questionnaire is reviewed by someone who works in the language.

Arabic, measured

Three candidates rendered at 100px against Manrope, whose line box is 137.

FaceLine boxvs ManropeInkVerdict
IBM Plex Sans Arabic151+10%76chosen
Cairo187+36%73breaks the density contract
Noto Sans Arabic211+54%78breaks the density contract
IBM Plex Sans Arabic · 600
مجهّزون للتنفيذ
نحن لا نبيع ورش عمل، بل نجعل الفرق قادرة على التنفيذ. كل برنامج ينتهي بمُخرَج قابل للاستخدام.

Arabic runs set at 0.95em of the Latin size — measured ink height is 76 against Manrope's cap of 72 — with line-height raised by 0.1. RTL locales add 10% to every row height in the density contract. A 28px dense row becomes 31px. This is a locale variable, not a redesign.

09 · Experience

What mirrors, and what does not

Mirrors

  • layout and reading order
  • the rail (side column moves right)
  • nav edges and selection edges
  • progress and the stepper
  • chevrons and back arrows

Does not mirror

  • the 会 mark — it is calligraphy, not an icon
  • numerals and the score meter fill (numbers read left to right in both)
  • charts with a time axis
  • logos and wordmarks of any kind
  • media controls

Logical properties, everywhere

Logical properties everywhere: margin-inline-start, padding-inline, border-inline-start, inset-inline. A single margin-left in a shared component is a bug that only appears in Arabic.

The 会 mark never mirrors. It is calligraphy, not an icon — a reversed brush stroke is not a mirrored logo, it is a wrong character. Numerals and the score meter do not mirror either: numbers read left to right in both directions.

Two products

The platform is desktop-first: it is a working tool used beside other windows. The questionnaire is mobile-first: it is met once, often on a phone, often by someone who will never open the platform again. They are different products and are built to different defaults.

Responsive

<600pxquestionnaire and reading only. The scorecard becomes a list, the table becomes rows, the sidebar becomes a bottom bar.
600-1023pxsingle working column, sidebar collapsed to 64px
1024-1439pxsidebar plus one working column
1440px+sidebar, working column and a detail drawer, all at once

The rule that breaks PDFs

Every breakpoint is `@media screen and (...)`. A bare media query fires during PDF export and collapses every column.

Never

hiding a control on small screens without moving it somewhere reachable. A feature that disappears on a phone has not been made responsive, it has been removed.

Below 600px the dense and compact scales collapse to comfortable. A 28px row is a desk decision; on a phone it is a target nobody can hit.
